sections.heading: C — Distractions and Driving Challenges (Section 11)
sections.markdown:
## C — Distractions and Driving Challenges (Section 11)
Emphasis: hazard response; pedagogic emphasis only, no official weights.

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
When an in-car distraction upsets control, pull to the roadside and stop before fixing it [A01].
Why it matters: panic fixes cause run-off-road crashes.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
A first road-rage conviction can bring a court-ordered license suspension of one year [A01].
Why it matters: key legal penalty.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A02
Near animals by the road, slow down, stay in lane, and do not swerve to miss them [A02].
Why it matters: swerving raises injury risk.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A02
If your car breaks down in the desert, stay with the vehicle and do not wander away [A02].
Why it matters: desert survival rule.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A03
Tired drivers should stop, take a short sleep break, and avoid late-night driving [A03].
Why it matters: fatigue slows sight and reactions.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A04
Never drive through a flooded road; turn around, find another route, or wait on high ground [A04].
Why it matters: hidden washouts and stalls.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A04
Shallow-looking floodwater can hide dips and washed-away pavement, so do not try to cross it [A04].
Why it matters: depth illusion trap.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A05
Work-zone signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols, and fines for speeding there are at least doubled [A05].
Why it matters: recognition plus penalty.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A06
On narrow downhill stretches, yield to vehicles coming uphill and never coast in neutral [A06].
Why it matters: mountain right-of-way plus control.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A06
At night, dim high beams before closing within the set oncoming and following gaps and add following time [A06].
Why it matters: glare control rule.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A07
When rear wheels skid right, steer right; when they skid left, steer left, without hard braking [A07].
Why it matters: core skid recovery.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A08
If the car enters water, act at once: belt off, window down, climb out, and pause for current check [A08].
Why it matters: seconds-long float window.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0073]

Misconceptions: swerving saves animals; floodwater can be judged by eye; high beams help in fog; braking hard fixes a skid.
Mnemonics: SIDE (Stay with desert car, In-lane for animals, Dim at night, Ease off skid).
Glossary: hydroplaning; black ice; road rage; work zone; rumble strip.
High-yield ranked: road-rage penalty; flood never-cross; skid steering; night dimming; desert stay-with-car.
